dedupe_keys.name: water focused social accounting matrix wf sam for jordan 2015

description: This social accounting matrix describes Jordan's economy in 2015 with the water sector disaggregated at micro-account level, so that computable general equilibrium models can trace how water utilities, irrigation and water users interact with the rest of the economy, for example the 12 percent of municipal water spending that goes on electricity. It has 155 accounts, including 57 activities, 63 commodities, 13 factors, ten household groups and government tax and subsidy accounts, and was built from the 2015 Jordan SAM of Raouf and co-authors, audited General Budget Department allocations to water utilities and Ministry of Water and Irrigation cash flows, balanced by cross entropy. Researchers at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin published it on Zenodo as a free download of one Excel workbook under CC BY 4.0 (January 2023). Coverage is national for a single year. Caveats: it is a 2015 snapshot and balancing adjusts the source figures. Simulation uses: economy-wide assessment of water pricing, supply investment and drought adaptation in optimisation and capacity planning studies of a water-scarce country. Related records: none catalogued yet.
